notes: Lowe's Home Decor (lowes.com/c/Home-decor). Same access situation and same 'helix' curated-listing microservice as bs70.json (see that file's notes for the full access-tier account: standard /c/ and /pl/ paths are Akamai-blocked this session, confirmed twice; sitemap.xml/robots.txt/the helix app at /best-sellers/, /new-releases/, /top-rated/ are not blocked). TARGET TERM MAPPING: the brief's target-term list does not literally include 'New Releases', but Lowe's own site names this exact concept 'New Releases' (title 'Lowe's New Releases: Home Decor') and it is functionally identical to 'Latest Arrivals'/'Newly Added' -- a curated top-N list of the newest products in a department, reached via the same helix app and URL-id pattern as Best Sellers/Top Rated. Judged a genuine synonym of New Arrivals per Sec 3's 'local-language equivalents' allowance (this is the site's own English-language term for the concept, just a different chosen word); recorded as a plain (unflagged) match, not an ambiguous-collection case, since it is a real curated product listing (not an editorial/campaign page) and its own meta copy explicitly frames it as 'most popular Home Decor available now' newest-stock listing. Found via newreleases0.xml sitemap (3543 URLs, one per category node sitewide, same mechanical pattern as bestsellers0.xml/toprated0.xml) grepped for '/home-decor/' -> department-root URL https://www.lowes.com/new-releases/home-decor/4294935484 (same category id 4294935484 as the rest of Home Decor). QTY VERIFICATION (exhaustion, ignoring the page's own unreliable embedded itemCount field, same known-bad field as documented in bs70.json/notes/70.md): page 1 (offset=0) productList array contains exactly 24 product objects; page 5 (?offset=96) contains exactly 4; totalPages=5, pageArray=[24,48,72,96] -> 96+4=100, matching the page's own meta-description claim 'Find the top 100 most popular Home Decor available now.' exactly. SUB-STRUCTURE DECISION: identical reasoning to bs70.json -- new-releases/{category-path}/{id} exists for every category node sitewide (3543 total, mechanical per-category feature, not a curated nav taxonomy), so only the single Home Decor department-level row is emitted, matching this company's site-root scope.
